rounds.text: Master Components Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental growth, achieving a 5-year sales CAGR of 41% [E14], TTM sales growth of 75% [E16], and TTM profit growth of 125% [E19], supported by a supportive Capital Goods sector tailwind [E60, E62]. This expansion is paired with strong profitability, featuring an ROCE of 26.6% [E12] and ROE of 22.4% [E13] that substantially outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10], alongside working capital requirements dropping from 64.7 days to 47.5 days [E53]. Despite profit growth outpacing 1-year share price growth by 111% [E50] and a top relative-strength rating of 100 [E44], valuation remains compressed at an EV/EBITDA of 10.11x versus the sector benchmark of 13.98x [E11], while a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 758 provides a 47.2% margin of safety [E38, E39]. Institutional validation is building as domestic institutions accumulated a 2.85% position from zero [E36], backed by conservative balance sheet leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E32]. Conceded: cash conversion was weak at 0.30x for Mar 2026 [E28], pushing free cash flow to Rs -3.31 Cr [E30] as borrowings rose to Rs 10.86 Cr [E33]. However, a reverse DCF shows today's price implies just 9.2% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case [E40], underpinning a rules-based score of 94 out of 100 [E54].

While headline growth figures look impressive, a deep disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation introduces severe underlying risk [E28]. Cash conversion for Mar 2026 sits at a dismal 0.30x, with operating cash flow representing a mere 18% of operating profit, pointing directly to potential issues in receivables or accruals [E28, E31]. Consequently, free cash flow has plunged into negative territory at Rs -3.31 Cr for Mar 2026 [E30]. This cash crunch coincides with a sharp escalation in borrowings, which surged to Rs 10.86 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 4.01 Cr a year prior [E33]. Furthermore, structural quality is called into question by the inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends [E26, E27], alongside an explicit rules-based screen warning that earnings growth is decelerating [E59]. Insider behavior also adds caution, as promoters have steadily reduced their stake from 72.45% in Sep 2023 to 67.10% by Mar 2026 [E35]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16].

While the bear flags a cash conversion ratio of 0.30x for Mar 2026 [E28], operating cash flow was positive at Rs 2.24 Cr [E29], and the company's working capital requirements have actually improved by narrowing from 64.7 days down to 47.5 days [E53]. Conceded: borrowings increased to Rs 10.86 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33], yet the resulting debt-to-equity ratio remains a healthy and conservatively financed 0.30x [E32]. Although margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E26, E27], the operating margin itself expanded to 19% in the Mar 2026 quarter compared to 17% in the year-ago period [E25]. Conceded: promoters trimmed their stake to 67.10% by Mar 2026 [E35], but domestic institutions stepped in to increase their holdings to 2.85% [E36]. Finally, despite the screen's warning of decelerating earnings growth [E59], trailing twelve-month profit growth remains extraordinary at 125% [E19], backed by robust rules-based screen fundamentals scoring 94 out of 100 [E54].

Conceded: operating cash flow was positive at Rs 2.24 Cr [E29] and debt-to-equity is conservatively financed at 0.30x [E32]. However, the bull glosses over the severe cash generation collapse where cash conversion sits at a dismal 0.30x and operating cash flow represents only 18% of operating profit, exposing a massive gap between reported profits and actual cash realized [E28, E31], which directly drives a negative free cash flow of Rs -3.31 Cr [E30]. Conceded: the quarterly operating margin ticked up to 19% [E25], but the underlying stability is compromised by a yearly and quarterly trend explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E26, E27]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased holdings [E36], yet promoters have steadily reduced their skin in the game from 72.45% down to 67.10% [E35]. Finally, while trailing twelve-month profit growth looks impressive [E19], the rules-based screen itself flashes a direct warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E59].

Conceded: the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E26, E27], and promoters reduced holdings to 67.10% [E35]. Conceded: the rules-based screen notes decelerating earnings growth [E59]. However, this profit growth is built on a phenomenal base, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reaching 125% and 5-year sales growth at 41% [E16, E19]. Furthermore, domestic institutions have stepped in to increase their stake by 2.85% to 2.85%, showing institutional confidence that offsets promoter reduction [E36]. The business continues to generate solid operating cash flow of Rs 2.24 Cr [E29], maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E32], and operates inside a robust capital goods sector tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E60].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reaches 125% and 5-year sales growth is 41% [E16, E19]. Conceded: operating cash flow stands at Rs 2.24 Cr [E29] and debt-to-equity is a conservative 0.30x [E32]. Conceded: the capital goods sector holds a tailwind score of +1.04 [E60] and domestic institutions increased their stake to 2.85% [E36]. However, pointing to phenomenal growth rates ignores the explicit rules-based warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E59]. Furthermore, citing Rs 2.24 Cr in operating cash flow obscures the severe operational strain of a negative free cash flow of Rs -3.31 Cr [E30]. Institutional participation at 2.85% is modest at best, and does not cancel out the persistent insider liquidation that saw promoter holdings drop by 5.35 percentage points to 67.10% [E35]. Finally, relying on sector tailwinds fails to justify a valuation trading at a P/B of 4.51x against a sector benchmark of just 2.58x [E7].
